scenarios.name: Eurasian Detente & Export Recovery
scenarios.description: Intensified diplomatic engagement between major economic powers (likely US-China and broader G20 framework) leads to normalized trade relations, reduced export barriers, and stimulus in global supply chains. This would reduce trade tensions, allowing U.S. exports to recover while restoring Chinese and allied supply-chain networks to manufacturing hubs.

impacts.explanation: Broader access to faster- growing markets and fewer tariff walls would lift merchandise exports.
tetlockCommandments: Break seemingly intractable problems into tractable sub-problems

impacts.explanation: Export-led demand recovery, global production normalization, and better terms of trade boost domestic output.
tetlockCommandments: Strike the right balance between under- and overreacting to evidence

scenarios.reasoning: Diplomatic breakthroughs are historically correlated with cyclical recoveries, but the current inflationary environment makes any export-driven reflationary impulse uncertain. Base rate from post-cold-war trade liberalization suggests a 15–25% historical chance of such detente but the de-globalization wave of 2025–2026 lowers this.

scenarios.name: Persistent Geopolitical Conflict Escalation
scenarios.description: Heightened conflict in Eastern Europe or Asia expands to direct confrontation involving resource-producing economies, disrupting energy flows, creating refugees, and imposing sustained sanctions on the U.S. or its allies. Escalation raises oil and commodity prices, fragnlizes trade corridors, and forces monetary contraction.

impacts.explanation: Higher energy import costs feed immediately into CPI; refugee flows disrupt food systems; hawkish central bank policy follows for risk management.
Central banks preemptively cut to defend domestic purchasing power as inflation rises.
Sanctions and energy shocks suppress output; trade rerouted away from the U.S.; uncertainty slows investment.
tetlockCommandments: Look for the clashing causal forces at work in each problem

scenarios.reasoning: The price of major oil shocks historically triggers terminal recessions with ~60% correlations with GDP, but probability weighs smaller shocks more heavily given current Fed posture. My Bayesian prior puts only 18% on this event though I note conflict has some effect in Turkey/Iran patterns.

scenarios.name: Global Financial Instability Triggered by Sovereign Debt Stress
scenarios.description: A major sovereign debt restructuring in a core G7 member (e.g., Italy or Belgium) becomes systemic via spread blowouts or contagion, producing loss-nroncent financing conditions and triggering a global credit crunch. UST bonds volatility climbs, and Treasury issuance, despite its safety, is overwhelmed by flight capital exits.

impacts.explanation: Direct disruption to global trade finance; interbank freeze reduces business credit; asymmetric shock to manufacturing.
